mainTopic: Rare words learned from everyday speech, and which שופר (straight or curved) is used on ראש השנה, fast days, and the יובל
overview: The amud opens by finishing the גמרא's collection of stories about rare words. The Sages learned these meanings from everyday speech. לוי did not understand the word 'קבען', and the בית המדרש explained that it means 'robbed', proving it from a פסוק in מלאכי. Next, the Sages learned four words (סירוגין, חלוגלוגות, סלסלה, and טאטא) from how רבי's maidservant spoke. רבה בר בר חנה learned that 'יהב' means a load from an Arab traveler. Then a new משנה describes the שופר used in the מקדש. On ראש השנה it was a straight ibex horn plated with gold. On fast days it was a curved ram's horn plated with silver. Whichever instrument is the main מצוה of the day blows longer. The משנה also teaches that the יובל's יום הכפורים is like ראש השנה, while רבי יהודה says ראש השנה uses rams' horns and the יובל uses ibex horns. In the גמרא, רבי לוי rules that curved שופרות are used on ראש השנה, and the גמרא explains that he follows רבי יהודה only on that point. Finally, the גמרא explains the root of the dispute: the curved or straight shape of the שופר matches whether a person should bend or straighten his mind on that day.

steps.title: לוי hears an unfamiliar word and asks about it
steps.stepSummary: A man tells לוי 'קבען פלניא.' לוי does not understand the word, so he goes to ask in the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'So-and-so קבען me.' He did not know what the man was saying to him. He went and asked in the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues a story already in progress: a man complained to לוי using a word לוי did not know. This step sets up the question that the בית המדרש will answer next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point of this collection is that some words were only understood from local speech. Here the unclear word is 'קבען.' לוי does the natural thing and brings the question to the בית המדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: He did קבע to me (the unclear word; later explained as 'robbed me')

phrases.english: So-and-so did keva'a to me.
phrases.notes: Continues the story of לוי earlier; this is the man's complaint.

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה יָדַע מַאי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He (לוי) did not know what he was saying to him.
He came and asked in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲוָה יָדַע מַאי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of stories about rare words on the previous amud.

steps.title: The study hall explains: it means 'robbed,' with a proof verse
steps.stepSummary: The בית המדרש tells לוי that 'קבען' means 'he robbed me,' and proves it from the פסוק 'היקבע אדם אלהים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He told you 'a robber' (that someone robbed him), as it is written: 'Will a man rob God?'
steps.whatsHappening: The בית המדרש answers לוי's question. The word means 'robbed,' and a פסוק in מלאכי shows that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works because the same root, קבע, appears in the פסוק, where it clearly means stealing: people were 'robbing' God of תרומות and מעשרות. So the word is a real Hebrew word for גזל that was simply not in common use where לוי lived.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: They said to him: He told you 'robber' (that someone robbed him).
phrases.notes: Meaning: the man was saying that So-and-so robbed him.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Will a man rob God?' etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'קבען' means 'robbed,' as shown by the פסוק 'היקבע אדם אלהים.'

steps.title: רבא from Barnish: I would have figured it out by asking
steps.stepSummary: רבא מברניש tells רב אשי that if he had been there, he would have asked the man questions about what happened, and that way he would have understood the word on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא מברניש said to רב אשי: If I had been there, I would have said to him: How did he קבעך? With what did he קבעך? And why did he קבעך? And from that I would have known on my own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מברניש suggests a smarter method than going to the בית המדרש: ask the man for details. This quietly criticizes how לוי handled it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The questions 'how, with what, and why' would bring out the facts of the story. From the facts, the meaning of the word would become obvious, for example 'he took my coat.' The implied challenge is: why did לוי not just do this?

keyTerms.meaning: רבא from the place called Barnish
And by itself; on my own

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִבַּרְנִישׁ לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava from Barnish said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲוַאי הָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: If I had been there, I would have said to him:
How did he keva'a you? With what did he keva'a you?
And why did he keva'a you?
And from that I would have known on my own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוַאי הָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on לוי's method of finding the meaning.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's choice to ask the בית המדרש instead of questioning the man himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Asking for the details of the event would have revealed the meaning directly, so there seems to have been no need to go to the בית המדרש.

steps.title: Why לוי did not ask: he thought it was about an איסור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that לוי thought the man was talking about an איסור, not about money, so questions like 'how, with what, and why' would not have helped.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he (לוי) thought: he was telling him about a matter of איסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends לוי. He did not ask those questions because he thought the man was asking about something forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Questions like 'with what did he do it to you?' only fit a case of ממון, where one person harmed another. לוי assumed the man was asking a halachic question about an איסור, so those questions would not have made sense. That is why going to the בית המדרש was the reasonable step.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter of prohibition (איסור), not of money

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'קבען' means 'robbed' (from 'היקבע אדם אלהים'). רבא מברניש would have figured it out from the details, but לוי thought it was an איסור question, where such questions would not help.

phrases.english: But he (לוי) thought:
He was telling him about a matter of prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied criticism of לוי in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the assumption לוי was working with
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי could easily have learned the meaning by asking about the facts.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי assumed it was an איסור question, where 'how, with what, and why' questions would not reveal anything, so he had to ask the בית המדרש.

steps.title: The maidservant explains the word סירוגין
steps.stepSummary: The Sages did not know what 'סירוגין' meant. They heard רבי's maidservant say it to Sages coming in a few at a time, so they learned it means 'at intervals.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages did not know what 'סירוגין' means. They heard the maidservant of רבי's house, who saw the Sages coming in group after group, say to them: 'How long will you come in סירוגין סירוגין?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story in the same series about rare words. The meaning of 'סירוגין' (a word found in a משנה) was learned from how the maidservant used it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages were coming in separately, a few at a time, and she described that as 'סירוגין.' So the word means 'with breaks in between,' or 'at intervals.'

keyTerms.meaning: At intervals; with breaks in between
Group by group; in separate parts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse 'סירוגין' with the word in step 1. Each story here is about a different word, and each is learned in its own way.

phrases.english: The Sages did not know what 'seirugin' means.
They heard the maidservant of Rabbi's house
who saw the Sages
entering group by group,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לְהוּ: עַד מָתַי אַתֶּם נִכְנָסִין
phrases.english: she said to them: How long will you keep entering
seirugin seirugin (at intervals)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new example in the same series of stories about rare words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'סירוגין' means 'at intervals,' learned from the maidservant's speech.

steps.title: The maidservant explains the word חלוגלוגות
steps.stepSummary: The Sages did not know what 'חלוגלוגות' meant. They heard the maidservant say it to a man scattering purslane, so they learned it means purslane.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages did not know what 'חלוגלוגות' means. One day they heard the maidservant of רבי's house, who saw a man scattering his purslane, say to him: 'How long will you scatter your חלוגלוגות?'
steps.whatsHappening: Another word in the series is explained the same way. A plant name was learned from the maidservant's everyday speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man was scattering 'פרפחינא,' the Aramaic word for purslane, and she called it 'חלוגלוגות.' So the Hebrew word in the משניות means purslane.

phrases.english: The Sages did not know what 'chaloglogot' means.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד שַׁמְעוּהָ לְאַמְּתָא דְבֵי רַבִּי
phrases.english: One day they heard the maidservant of Rabbi's house
who saw a certain man
who was scattering his purslane,
she said to him: How long
will you scatter your chaloglogot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next example in the same series, following the same pattern.

steps.title: The maidservant explains סלסלה in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The Sages did not know what 'סלסלה' in the פסוק 'סלסלה ותרוממך' meant. They heard the maidservant tell a man curling his hair 'how long will you מסלסל your hair,' so they learned it means 'turn it over.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages did not know what 'סלסלה ותרוממך' means. One day they heard the maidservant of רבי's house speaking to a man who was curling his hair. She said to him: 'How long will you curl your hair?'
steps.whatsHappening: The next example explains a word in a פסוק in משלי. Its meaning was learned from the maidservant's comment about curling hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'מסלסל' means turning and curling hair over and over, the פסוק means: keep turning Torah wisdom over and reviewing it, and it will raise you up. This time a פסוק is explained, not just a word from a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Turn it over (review it), and it will exalt you (משלי ד:ח)

steps.whatToRemember: The words סירוגין, חלוגלוגות and סלסלה were all learned from how רבי's maidservant used them in daily speech. The next step adds one more word from her. Ordinary language can reveal the meaning of words in משנה and פסוקים.

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי רַבָּנַן מַאי: ״סַלְסְלֶהָ וּתְרוֹמְמֶךָּ״.
phrases.english: The Sages did not know what 'salseleha and it will exalt you' means.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד שַׁמְעוּהָ לְאַמְּתָא דְבֵי רַבִּי
phrases.english: One day they heard the maidservant of Rabbi's house
who was speaking to a certain man
who was turning over (curling) his hair,
she said to him: How long
will you keep curling your hair?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי רַבָּנַן מַאי: ״סַלְסְלֶהָ וּתְרוֹמְמֶךָּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third maidservant story, continuing the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'סלסלה' means 'turn it over' (keep reviewing Torah wisdom), as in curling hair.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains a well-known פסוק about learning: Torah grows in a person who keeps turning it over and reviewing it.

steps.title: Learning the meaning of the word for sweeping
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן did not understand 'וטאטאתיה במטאטא השמד'. They heard רבי's maidservant tell her friend to take a broom and sweep the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages did not know what 'and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction' means. One day they heard the maidservant of רבי's house telling her friend: 'Take the broom and sweep the house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of hard words the רבנן learned from רבי's maidservant. This time the word is 'טאטא', which means to sweep, and 'מטאטא', which means a broom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as the earlier steps. A hard word in a פסוק is cleared up by hearing a simple household use of the same root. The maidservant said 'טאטיתא' (broom) and 'טאטי' (sweep), so the פסוק means God will sweep בבל away like dirt with a broom.

phrases.english: The Sages did not know
what 'and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction' means.
phrases.notes: ישעיהו יד:כג, about the destruction of בבל

phrases.english: One day they heard
the maidservant of רבי's house
who was saying to her friend:
Take the broom and sweep the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another entry in the same list of words learned from רבי's maidservant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'טאטא' means to sweep, and 'מטאטא' means a broom.

steps.title: Learning that 'יהבך' means your load
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן did not understand 'יהבך' in 'השלך על ה׳ יהבך'. רבה בר בר חנה learned its meaning when an Arab told him to put his load on the camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages did not know what 'cast your יהב upon ה׳ and He will sustain you' means. רבה בר בר חנה said: One day I was traveling with a certain Arab, and I was carrying a load. He said to me: 'Take your יהב and throw it on my camel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with another hard word, but this time the source is different. רבה בר בר חנה learned the meaning from an Arab merchant on the road, not from רבי's maidservant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Arab used 'יהביך' for the load רבה בר בר חנה was carrying. This shows that 'יהבך' in the פסוק means 'your burden'. So the פסוק teaches: throw your burdens onto ה׳, the way you would put a heavy pack on a camel, and He will carry you.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה בר בר חנה was there when the רבנן asked. The גמרא simply attaches his personal story here because it explains the same unclear word.

phrases.english: The Sages did not know
what 'Cast your load upon ה׳'
and He will sustain you' means.
רבה בר בר חנה said:
One day I was traveling
with a certain Arab,
I was carrying a load,
and he said to me:
Take your load and throw it on my camel.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי רַבָּנַן מַאי ״הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה׳ יְהָבְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final entry in the list of hard words. The source of the meaning changes from the maidservant to an Arab traveler.
steps.whatToRemember: This whole section teaches that even great חכמים learned the meaning of words in משנה and תנ״ך from simple everyday speech. They heard it from a maidservant at home and from an Arab on the road.

steps.title: The שופר and trumpets used on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes the ראש השנה setup in the מקדש. It used a straight horn of a יעל with a gold mouth, plus two חצוצרות on the sides. The שופר blew long because it is the main מצוה of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שופר of ראש השנה was made from the horn of a יעל (ibex). It was straight, and its mouthpiece was covered with gold. There were two trumpets on the sides. The שופר blew a long blast and the trumpets blew a short blast, because the מצוה of the day is with the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes what kind of שופר was blown in the בית המקדש on ראש השנה, and how it was blown together with trumpets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three details: the material (a straight יעל horn), the decoration (gold on the mouthpiece), and the trumpets placed on either side. The key rule is that the שופר's sound lasted longer than the trumpets. This made it clear that the שופר is the main מצוה of ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: the משנה (a new one begins here)

steps.confusionAlert: This setup with gold and trumpets was done in the בית המקדש. It is not the normal שופר everyone uses today.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The shofar of Rosh HaShana
is of an ibex, straight,
and its mouth is plated with gold,
and two trumpets at the sides.
The shofar blows long
and the trumpets blow short,
because the מצוה of the day is with the shofar.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שׁוֹפָר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁל יָעֵל פָּשׁוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A brand-new משנה. It is not connected to the list of word meanings that came before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה the שופר is the main מצוה, so it blows longer than the trumpets.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that whichever instrument is 'the מצוה of the day' blows longer is the key to the whole משנה. The next part flips this exact rule for fast days.

steps.title: The setup reversed on fast days
steps.stepSummary: On fast days the setup was different. They used curved ram horns with silver mouths, with the trumpets in the middle. The trumpets blew long because they are the main מצוה of a fast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: On fast days they used שופרות from male animals (rams), which are curved. Their mouths were covered with silver, and two trumpets stood in the middle. The שופר blew short and the trumpets blew long, because the מצוה of the day is with the trumpets.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now compares ראש השנה with public fast days (תעניות). Almost every detail is reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The changes are: curved ram horns instead of straight יעל horns, silver instead of gold, and trumpets in the middle instead of on the sides. Most important, the trumpets now blow long and the שופר blows short, because on a fast day the trumpets are the main מצוה. The principle stays the same: the main מצוה of the day gets the longer sound.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule is the same on both days: whichever instrument is the main מצוה of that day blows longer. On ראש השנה that is the שופר. On fast days it is the חצוצרות.

phrases.english: And on fast days
with those of rams, curved,
and their mouths plated with silver,
and two trumpets in the middle.
The shofar blows short
and the trumpets blow long,
because the מצוה of the day is with the trumpets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second half of the same משנה. It reverses the ראש השנה setup for fast days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On fast days the חצוצרות are the main מצוה, so they blow longer than the שופר.

steps.title: The יובל's יום הכפורים is like ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that the יום הכפורים of the יובל year is the same as ראש השנה for the שופר blasts and the ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The יובל is the same as ראש השנה for the שופר blowing and for the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section of the משנה compares the יובל to ראש השנה. Both days get the same shofar blasts and the same special ברכות in the תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יובל year, the שופר is blown on יום הכפורים to announce freedom for slaves and the return of fields. This first opinion (the תנא קמא) says that day is treated exactly like ראש השנה, including which שופר is used.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jubilee year (every 50th year), announced by a שופר on יום הכפורים
Is the same as / equal to
Blessings (here, the special additions to the עמידה)

phrases.english: The Jubilee is the same as Rosh Hashanah
phrases.notes: This means the יום הכפורים of the Jubilee year.

phrases.english: for the shofar blowing and for the blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה about the shofar setup in the מקדש, now comparing the יובל to ראש השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום הכפורים of the יובל is treated like ראש השנה for shofar and blessings, so it uses the same straight ibex shofar.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: rams on ראש השנה, ibexes in the יובל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees: ראש השנה uses ram horns, while the יובל uses ibex horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: On ראש השנה we blow with horns of rams, and in the יובל years with horns of ibexes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on the first opinion. He says the two days do NOT use the same kind of shofar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, ראש השנה used a straight ibex horn (Step 10). רבי יהודה switches this around: ראש השנה gets a ram's horn, which is curved, and the יובל gets an ibex horn.

keyTerms.meaning: Rams (male sheep), whose horns are curved

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
On Rosh Hashanah we blow with horns of rams,
and in the Jubilee years with horns of ibexes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראש השנה uses ram horns and the יובל uses ibex horns.

steps.title: רבי לוי: curved שופרות for ראש השנה and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי rules that ראש השנה and יום הכפורים use curved שופרות, and the rest of the year uses straight ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי לוי said: The מצוה of ראש השנה and of יום הכפורים is with curved שופרות, and that of the rest of the year is with straight ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from the אמורא רבי לוי about which shape of shofar to use on each occasion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יום הכפורים' here means the יום הכפורים of the יובל year. 'The rest of the year' means fast days, when שופרות were also blown. רבי לוי says: curved for ראש השנה and יום הכפורים, straight for fast days.

keyTerms.meaning: The rest of the year (here, fast days)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'כל השנה' means every day of the year. It means the other times the שופר was blown, mainly the fast days.

phrases.english: Gemara: Rabbi Levi said:
The מצוה of Rosh Hashanah
and of Yom Kippur is with curved shofars,
phrases.notes: The יום הכפורים of the יובל year.

phrases.english: and that of the rest of the year is with straight ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה with an אמורא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Curved shofars for ראש השנה and the יובל's יום הכפורים; straight shofars for the rest of the year.

steps.title: But the משנה said ראש השנה used a straight ibex horn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי לוי from the משנה, which says the ראש השנה shofar was a straight ibex horn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: The שופר of ראש השנה was of an ibex, straight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי לוי's ruling. The משנה we just learned says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10's משנה said ראש השנה used a straight ibex horn. רבי לוי said ראש השנה needs a curved shofar. An אמורא should not contradict a משנה, so this is a serious question.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה! (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the Mishnah:
The shofar of Rosh Hashanah
was of an ibex, straight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי לוי's ruling from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי לוי's ruling that ראש השנה requires a curved shofar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה (Step 10) explicitly says the ראש השנה shofar was a straight ibex horn, which contradicts רבי לוי.

steps.title: רבי לוי follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי holds like רבי יהודה, who says in a ברייתא that ראש השנה used curved ram horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it like this תנא, as it was taught: רבי יהודה says: On ראש השנה they would blow with curved rams' horns, and in the יובל years with ibex horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי לוי is not contradicting everyone. He is following a different תנא, רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in Step 10 is the view of the תנא קמא. A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying the ראש השנה rams' horns were curved. So רבי לוי has a תנא to rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this תנא (he follows this opinion)
As was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He said it in line with this Tanna,
as it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
On Rosh Hashanah they would blow
with curved rams' horns,
and in the Jubilee years with ibex horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי לוי seemed to contradict the משנה with no support.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי לוי follows רבי יהודה, who says ראש השנה used curved rams' horns.

steps.title: Why not just say the הלכה follows רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי לוי made his own long statement instead of simply saying 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him say: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the way רבי לוי worded his ruling. If he simply agrees with רבי יהודה, he could have said so in a few words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי's statement seems to repeat what רבי יהודה already said. The גמרא wants to know what his own wording adds.

phrases.english: Then let him say: The halachah follows Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in Step 16 to question רבי לוי's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי לוי's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he follows רבי יהודה, his own longer statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: He agrees with רבי יהודה only about ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה' would suggest agreeing with him about the יובל too. רבי לוי's wording shows that he agrees only about ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you had said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, I would have thought he holds like רבי יהודה even about the יובל. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי לוי used his own wording. A short 'הלכה כרבי יהודה' would have been misleading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says the יובל uses an ibex horn. רבי לוי holds that the יובל's יום הכפורים uses a curved shofar. So he agrees with רבי יהודה only partly, and his own wording makes that clear.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי לוי follows רבי יהודה ONLY on ראש השנה (curved), not on the יובל. That is why he gave his own ruling instead of saying 'הלכה כרבי יהודה.'

phrases.english: If you had said the halachah follows Rabbi Yehuda,
I would have thought:
even about the Jubilee too
he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the wording was needed (limiting the agreement)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A plain 'הלכה כרבי יהודה' would mean agreeing with him about the יובל too.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי לוי agrees with רבי יהודה only about ראש השנה, not about the יובל.

steps.title: What is the reasoning behind the dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind each side, and the next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know WHAT each side holds. Now the גמרא wants the underlying idea that leads each תנא to choose curved or straight.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asks for the root reason)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ruling to the reasoning behind the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Bending versus straightening the mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that on ראש השנה a person should bend (humble) his mind and on יום הכפורים straighten it. The תנא קמא holds the opposite: straighten on ראש השנה and bend on fast days.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds: On ראש השנה, the more a person bends his mind, the better; on יום הכפורים, the more he straightens his mind, the better. The other Sage holds: On ראש השנה, the more a person straightens his mind, the better; on fast days, the more he bends his mind, the better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the shape of the shofar matches the attitude a person should have on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A curved שופר stands for a bent, humbled heart, and a straight שופר for a straight, sincere heart. רבי יהודה says to bend on ראש השנה (curved ram) and straighten on יום הכפורים (straight ibex). The תנא קמא says to straighten on ראש השנה (straight ibex) and bend on fast days (curved rams, as in Step 11).
steps.whatToRemember: The shofar's shape reflects the mood of the day: curved means humbling yourself, straight means a straight, sincere heart. רבי יהודה and the תנא קמא disagree about which mood fits ראש השנה.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'מר' is רבי יהודה and the second 'מר' is the תנא קמא of the משנה. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: On Rosh Hashanah,
the more a person bends his mind,
the better;
and on Yom Kippur,
the more a person straightens his mind,
the better.
And the other Sage holds: On Rosh Hashanah,
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא of the משנה

phrases.english: the more a person straightens his mind,
the better;
and on fast days,
the more a person bends his mind,
the better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about which attitude fits ראש השנה. רבי יהודה says humble bending (curved shofar); the תנא קמא says straight sincerity (straight shofar), with bending saved for fast days.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the physical shape of the shofar carries meaning: it should match the inner attitude a person needs on that day.
